mainTopic: Do מצוות require intent? רבא's view, challenges from sources, and how בל תוסיף relates to intent and a מצוה's time
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבא's ruling that someone who blows שופר just for music still fulfills the מצוה, and the גמרא concludes that רבא holds מצות אין צריכות כוונה. It then tests this against a משנה about reading שמע and our משנה about hearing שופר outside a בית הכנסת. Each time, the required 'intent' is explained as something small: reading properly, or knowing the sound is a שופר and not a donkey. A ברייתא requiring the blower's intent is answered by saying he made rough, barking blasts. אביי then argues that if no intent is needed, sleeping in a סוכה on שמיני עצרת should break בל תוסיף, and רבא answers that בל תוסיף applies only within a מצוה's time. רב שמן בר אבא challenges this from a כהן who adds his own ברכה, which leads to the idea that a מצוה which can be repeated that day has the whole day as its time, discussed through a משנה about mixed sacrificial blood. Finally רבא gives another answer: fulfilling a מצוה needs no intent, and breaking בל תוסיף needs intent only outside the מצוה's time. The amud ends as רבי זירא begins an instruction to his attendant, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why רבא's שופר ruling is still a new teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why רבא's ruling about שופר teaches something new: the פסוק 'זכרון תרועה' might have suggested that intent is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, by שופר, the Torah writes 'a remembrance of blasts,' and this person was just blowing without any thought of the מצוה. So you might think he did not fulfill it. רבא teaches us that he did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its answer to 'isn't this obvious?' by explaining why the שופר case could have been different from the מצה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מצה, the Torah says 'eat,' and the person ate, so the action itself is enough. By שופר, the word 'זכרון' (remembrance) sounds like it needs mental focus, so blowing for music might not count. רבא teaches that even here, the act is enough without intent.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A remembrance of blasts' — the Torah's phrase describing ראש השנה (ויקרא כג:כד)
Someone doing an action without paying attention to its purpose, acting unawares
'It teaches us' — shows that a statement is adding something new
Merely, just

steps.confusionAlert: This is the second half of a 'מהו דתימא' (you might have thought) answer that started on the previous amud. The first half was about מצה ('the Torah said eat, and he ate'). 'אבל הכא' contrasts שופר with that case.

phrases.english: But here, 'a remembrance of blasts' is written,
phrases.notes: The word 'remembrance' suggests that awareness or focus is needed.

phrases.english: and this one is merely acting unawares —
phrases.notes: He was blowing for music, not for the מצוה.

phrases.english: so it teaches us [that he still fulfilled it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer, begun on the previous amud, to the question 'פשיטא' asked about רבא's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא — the ruling is needed to reject a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the word 'זכרון', you might think שופר requires intent, unlike מצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even by שופר, blowing without intent fulfills the מצוה.

steps.title: רבא holds that מצוות do not require intent
steps.stepSummary: From רבא's ruling, the גמרא infers his general position: מצות אין צריכות כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it turns out that רבא holds that מצוות do not need intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general rule from רבא's specific ruling about שופר. This sets up the challenges that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If blowing for music counts even under 'זכרון', then רבא clearly holds that the action alone fulfills the מצוה. This turns a single case into a broad principle, which can now be tested against other sources.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Apparently, it turns out' — introduces a conclusion drawn from what was said
He holds, he is of the opinion
מצוות do not require intent to fulfill them

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's position is מצות אין צריכות כוונה: doing the act is enough, even without intending to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the central debates in all of הלכה, and the rest of the sugya tests it against several משניות.

phrases.english: Apparently, Rava holds:
מצוות do not require intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general principle out of the explanation in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבא, מצות אין צריכות כוונה.

steps.title: Challenge from reading שמע in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from a משנה in ברכות: someone reading the שמע section in the Torah fulfills קריאת שמע only if he focused his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If someone was reading the Torah and the time to say שמע arrived while he was reading that section, then if he focused his heart, he fulfilled the מצוה; if not, he did not. Doesn't 'focused his heart' mean he intended to fulfill the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's view with a משנה that seems to require intent for קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is already saying the right words at the right time, yet the משנה says he fulfills the מצוה only if 'כוון לבו'. If that means intent to fulfill, then מצוות do require intent, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They challenged him' — an objection from a משנה or ברייתא
The time for reciting קריאת שמע
He focused his heart, he had intent
He fulfilled his obligation
'Is it not that…?' — suggests a reading of a source that works against someone
To fulfill the obligation

phrases.english: They challenged him: If one was reading in the Torah
phrases.notes: He was reading the section of שמע. The source is משנה ברכות ב:א.

phrases.english: and the time of reciting [Shema] arrived,
if he focused his heart — he fulfilled [the obligation],
and if not — he did not fulfill it.
Is it not that 'focused his heart' means: to fulfill [the מצוה]!
phrases.notes: If so, intent is required, against רבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the principle from step 2 against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that מצות אין צריכות כוונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes fulfilling the מצוה depend on 'כוון לבו', which seems to mean intent to fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: Answer: the intent is to read
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'כוון לבו' means he intended to read the words, not to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No — it means he intended to read.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by reading 'focused his heart' in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the intent the משנה requires is just intent to read, it says nothing about intent to fulfill a מצוה. רבא's view would then be untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: To read

phrases.english: No: [he focused his heart] to read.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כוון לבו' means intent to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כוון לבו' means intent to read the words.

steps.title: But he is already reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה already says he is reading, so what does 'intent to read' add?
steps.simpleTranslation: To read?! But he is already reading!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in step 4, because it seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה opens with 'היה קורא בתורה', so he is clearly reading. Requiring 'intent to read' would add nothing, so the answer looks forced.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But he is reading!' — a surprised objection

phrases.english: To read?! But he is reading!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'כוון לבו' as 'intent to read'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already describes him as reading, so 'intent to read' is redundant.

steps.title: He was reading to check the scroll
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is someone reading in order to proofread the ספר תורה, not to read in the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about someone reading in order to correct the scroll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which kind of 'reading' is meant, so the answer from step 4 works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone checking a scroll for mistakes looks at the letters and may not say the words properly. 'כוון לבו' then means he intended to actually read the words properly. That is intent to read, not intent to fulfill a מצוה, so רבא's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To proofread, to correct (a scroll)

steps.whatToRemember: The קריאת שמע משנה does not disprove רבא. The intent it requires is intent to read properly, in the case of someone proofreading.

phrases.english: [It refers] to one reading in order to correct [the scroll].
phrases.notes: He was checking letters, not reading the words properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 5 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The person was reading normally, so 'intent to read' adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was proofreading, so 'intent to read' properly is meaningful, and רבא's view stands.

steps.title: Challenge from hearing שופר or מגילה outside a בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second challenge from our משנה: someone who hears שופר or מגילה from outside a בית הכנסת fulfills the מצוה only if he focused his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone was passing behind a בית הכנסת, or his house was next to a בית הכנסת, and he heard the sound of the שופר or the reading of the מגילה, then if he focused his heart he fulfilled the מצוה, and if not he did not. Doesn't that mean he intended to fulfill the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new challenge to רבא, again arguing that 'כוון לבו' means intent to fulfill. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'intent to read' answer from step 6 cannot work, because this person is only listening. The משנה still says 'כוון לבו', which seems to mean intent to fulfill the מצוה. If so, this works against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear' — introduces a source as a proof or challenge
Synagogue
The sound of the שופר
The sound of the מגילה (מגילת אסתר) being read

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיָה עוֹבֵר אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: Come and hear: If one was passing behind a synagogue,
phrases.notes: This is from our משנה (ראש השנה 27b).

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ סָמוּךְ לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: or his house was next to the synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁמַע קוֹל שׁוֹפָר אוֹ קוֹל מְגִילָּה,
phrases.english: and he heard the sound of the shofar or the sound of the Megillah,
if he focused his heart — he fulfilled [the obligation],
and if not — he did not fulfill it.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, אִם כִּוֵּון לִבּוֹ לָצֵאת?
phrases.english: Is it not [that it means] if he focused his heart to fulfill [the מצוה]?
phrases.notes: The גמרא's answer appears next.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיָה עוֹבֵר אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a second challenge to רבא's principle is raised from a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that מצות אין צריכות כוונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The listener is not reading, so 'כוון לבו' cannot mean intent to read. It seems to mean intent to fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: The intent in our משנה is only intent to hear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from our משנה. 'כוון לבו' means he intended to hear the sound, not that he intended to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The משנה means he intended to hear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It says the 'focusing of the heart' in our משנה is only about intending to hear, not about intending to do the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, our משנה seemed to require real intent to fulfill the מצוה, which would contradict רבא. This answer makes the required intent much smaller: just a desire to hear the sound. That kind of intent fits with רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: No. This rejects the way the challenger read the source.
To hear. Here it means intent simply to hear the sound.

phrases.english: No, he intended to hear.
phrases.notes: The 'כוון לבו' of the משנה is redefined as intent to hear the sound, not intent to do the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7 by reinterpreting what 'כוון לבו' means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כוון לבו' meant intent to fulfill the מצוה, which would refute רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כוון לבו' means only intent to hear, which works with רבא.

steps.title: But the משנה already says he heard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה already says he heard the שופר, so 'intent to hear' seems to add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: To hear?! But he already heard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If the משנה already says he heard the sound, what does 'he intended to hear' add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of problem as Step 5. A condition must add something new. If 'intent to hear' just means 'he heard,' it repeats what the משנה already said.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely. A word that introduces a contradiction.
He heard. This is already written in the משנה.

phrases.english: To hear?! But he heard!
phrases.notes: The משנה already describes him as hearing the שופר, so intent to hear seems redundant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 8 as redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that 'כוון לבו' means intent to hear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already says he heard. A condition of 'intent to hear' would then add nothing.

steps.title: He thought it was just a donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the case is someone who heard the sound but thought it was a donkey braying. 'Intent to hear' means knowing it is a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought it was merely a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what 'intent to hear' adds. A person can hear the sound and still think it is just a donkey. He must know he is hearing a שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing the sound is not enough if he does not know what the sound is. The משנה excludes only someone who did not recognize it as a שופר. It does not require intent to fulfill the מצוה, so רבא still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought, or assumed.
A donkey.
Merely, just.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's view (no intent needed) does not mean a person can be totally unaware of what he heard. He must know it is a שופר. He just does not need intent to fulfill the מצוה.

phrases.english: He thought it was merely a donkey.
phrases.notes: He heard the sound but did not know it was a שופר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy problem of Step 9 by defining a case where someone hears without 'intent to hear'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hearing and 'intent to hear' are the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: One can hear a sound without knowing it is a שופר. The משנה requires that awareness, not intent for the מצוה.

steps.title: A ברייתא requires intent from both hearer and blower
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says both the hearer and the blower must have intent. The hearer case can be the 'donkey' case. But a blower without intent must be someone blowing for music, which shows the blower needs intent for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If the hearer intended but the blower did not, or the blower intended but the hearer did not, he has not fulfilled his obligation, until both the hearer and the blower intend. Granted, the case where the blower intended but the hearer did not can be someone who thought it was just a donkey. But the case where the hearer intended and the blower did not, how can it happen? Is it not someone blowing for music?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רבא again. It works through both halves of the ברייתא to show that one half seems to require real intent for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hearer half fits רבא through the donkey case. But a blower always knows he is blowing a שופר, so the donkey answer cannot work for him. The only clear case of a blower 'without intent' seems to be blowing for music, which means he needs intent to fulfill the מצוה. That goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a ברייתא or משנה.
The hearer.
The one who makes others hear: the blower.
Granted. This accepts one part before attacking another part.
How can you find this case?
For music or song.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: נִתְכַּוֵּון שׁוֹמֵעַ וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון מַשְׁמִיעַ,
phrases.english: He challenged him: If the hearer intended but the blower did not intend,
or the blower intended but the hearer did not intend,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יָצָא, עַד שֶׁיִּתְכַּוֵּון שׁוֹמֵעַ וּמַשְׁמִיעַ.
phrases.english: he has not fulfilled his obligation, until both the hearer and the blower intend.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא נִתְכַּוֵּון מַשְׁמִיעַ וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון שׁוֹמֵעַ —
phrases.english: Granted, where the blower intended but the hearer did not intend,
that is like someone who thought it was merely a donkey,
phrases.notes: This uses the answer from Step 10.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נִתְכַּוֵּון שׁוֹמֵעַ וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון מַשְׁמִיעַ —
phrases.english: but where the hearer intended and the blower did not intend,
how can you find this case?
Is it not where he blows for music!
phrases.notes: He knows it is a שופר but has no intent for the מצוה, and the ברייתא says this does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses Step 10's donkey answer for one half of the ברייתא and shows it cannot work for the other half.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a מצוה does not need intent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blower always knows he is blowing a שופר, so 'no intent' for him must mean no intent for the מצוה, for example blowing for music. The ברייתא says this fails, so intent is needed.

steps.title: Perhaps the blower just made barking sounds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The blower's 'lack of intent' can mean he blew sloppy, barking sounds instead of proper תקיעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he was making barking sounds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the ברייתא. It offers another way a blower can lack 'intent' that has nothing to do with intent for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 assumed the only possible case was blowing for music. Here the 'intent' the blower lacks is intent to produce proper blasts; he just made rough, barking noises. So the ברייתא is about blowing correctly, not about intending the מצוה, and רבא survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps. A word that offers another possible reading to reject a proof.
Making barking sounds: rough, improper blasts.

phrases.english: Perhaps he was making barking sounds.
phrases.notes: He did not blow properly. The required 'intent' is intent to blow correctly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 11 by offering another case of a blower 'without intent'.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ברייתא's blower case must be blowing for music.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenger missed another option: the blower lacked intent to produce proper sounds, not intent for the מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: So far, every challenge to רבא has been answered by making the required 'intent' something small: knowing it is a שופר (hearer) or blowing properly (blower). None of these is intent to fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: אביי: then sleeping in a סוכה on שמיני should earn lashes
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: if a מצוה counts without intent, then someone who sleeps in a סוכה on שמיני עצרת is adding to the מצוה and should get מלקות for בל תוסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But if so, one who sleeps in a סוכה on שמיני עצרת should receive lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new challenge to רבא from a different angle. If acts count as מצוות even without intent, sitting in a סוכה after סוכות should count as adding to the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the challenges said you need intent to fulfill a מצוה. אביי turns it around: if no intent is needed, then a מצוה act done at the wrong time also counts automatically. That would mean breaking בל תוסיף (adding to a מצוה) and deserving מלקות, which is clearly not the law.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so. It pushes a view to its unacceptable result.
The Eighth Day: שמיני עצרת, after the seven days of סוכות.
He should receive lashes (מלקות).
The prohibition against adding to a מצוה. It is assumed here, not written in the text.

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying sleeping in a סוכה on שמיני is forbidden by itself. His point is that under רבא's rule it would automatically count as an extra מצוה, which would break בל תוסיף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the debate from 'fulfilling' a מצוה to 'violating' one. It forces רבא to explain how an act without intent can count for one purpose and not for another.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But if so,
one who sleeps in the sukkah on the Eighth Day should receive lashes!
phrases.notes: Lashes for בל תוסיף, since the act would count as a מצוה even without intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא challenge is answered, אביי opens a new attack from the side of בל תוסיף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a מצוה does not need intent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a מצוה act counts without intent, then dwelling in a סוכה after its time counts as an extra מצוה and breaks בל תוסיף. That would mean מלקות for an ordinary act, which cannot be right.

steps.title: רבא: Adding to a מצוה only counts within its proper time
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers אביי: בל תוסיף applies only when you add to a מצוה during its proper time. Sleeping in a סוכה on שמיני עצרת is after the time of סוכה, so it is not בל תוסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Because I say that a person only transgresses בל תוסיף on מצוות when he adds to them during their proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's question from step 13. He says sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת is not a problem, because סוכות is already over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that if a מצוה counts even without intent, sitting in a סוכה on שמיני עצרת should automatically count as adding to the מצוה. רבא answers with a time limit: בל תוסיף only applies while the מצוה is still in force. On שמיני עצרת the מצוה of סוכה is finished, so nothing is being added to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against adding to a מצוה
In their proper time
Transgresses
Because I say (introduces the speaker's reasoning)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that a מצוה needs intent. He keeps his position that a מצוה counts without intent, and solves the סוכה problem with a different rule: time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a new principle, that בל תוסיף depends on the מצוה's time. The rest of this passage tests that principle.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: Because I say:
מצוות, one does not transgress on them (by adding)
except in their proper time.
phrases.notes: On שמיני עצרת, the time for סוכה has ended.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a limiting principle (a time boundary for בל תוסיף)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any repeat of a מצוה action, even after its time, would count as adding to the מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: בל תוסיף applies only within the מצוה's set time, so the סוכה on שמיני עצרת is no problem.

steps.title: Challenge from a כהן who adds his own blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא quotes a ברייתא: a כהן may not add his own ברכה to ברכת כהנים, because of לא תוסיפו. Once he has finished blessing, the time has passed. Yet the ברייתא still says he violated the prohibition. This contradicts רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא objected: Where do we learn that a כהן who goes up to the דוכן should not say, 'Since the Torah gave me permission to bless Israel, I will add a ברכה of my own, such as "May ה׳, the God of your fathers, increase you"'? The verse says: 'Do not add to the matter.' But here, once he has finished blessing, the time has passed, and the ברייתא still teaches that he transgressed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמן בר אבא attacks רבא's new rule. He brings a case where adding seems to happen after the מצוה's time, yet it still counts as בל תוסיף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids a כהן from tacking on an extra ברכה, based on the verse לא תוסיפו. The case sounds like the כהן has already finished ברכת כהנים, so the מצוה's time should be over. According to רבא, adding after the time should not be a problem, but the ברייתא treats it as a violation.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (usually from a תנאי source)
The platform where the כהנים stand to bless
Permission, authority
Do not add (the source verse for בל תוסיף)
And yet it teaches

phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba raised an objection:
From where do we know, for a kohen who goes up to the platform,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר: הוֹאִיל וְנָתְנָה לִי תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: that he should not say: Since the Torah gave me
permission to bless the Jewish people,
I will add one blessing of my own,
for example: 'May God, the God of your fathers, increase you'
phrases.notes: A verse from דברים א:יא, not part of ברכת כהנים.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'Do not add to the matter.'
But here, since he has already blessed,
its time has passed,
and yet it teaches that he transgressed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's time-based rule from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that בל תוסיף applies only within the מצוה's time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes adding after the ברכה is finished, which is after the time, yet it still counts as בל תוסיף.

steps.title: The כהן had not yet finished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a כהן who added his ברכה before finishing ברכת כהנים. That means he added during the מצוה's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he had not yet finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case. The כהן added his own ברכה in the middle, before completing the ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן is still in the middle of ברכת כהנים, the מצוה's time has not passed. So adding then is inside the time, and that fits רבא's rule exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows a source to a specific case)
Finished, completed

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With a case where he did not finish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שמן בר אבא's challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן added after finishing ברכת כהנים, which is after the time.
steps.terutzMaskana: He added before finishing, during the time, so it is בל תוסיף even according to רבא.

steps.title: But a ברייתא says he finished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: another ברייתא explicitly says the כהן had finished, so the 'did not finish' answer seems wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'He finished'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 16. A parallel ברייתא describes the כהן as having already finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 16 depended on the כהן not having finished. The wording 'סיים' in the parallel ברייתא seems to rule that out, which brings back the original challenge to רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: 'He finished'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case narrowing in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is a case where he did not finish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own wording says he finished, which contradicts the narrowing.

steps.title: He finished only one of the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'he finished' means he finished one ברכה, the first of the three verses of ברכת כהנים. Two are still left, so he is still within the מצוה's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He finished one ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets the word 'סיים' in a way that saves רבא. The כהן finished only one part of ברכת כהנים, not the whole thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת כהנים has three ברכות. If the כהן added his own ברכה after only the first, he is still in the middle of the מצוה. So the addition happened within its time, and רבא's rule holds.

keyTerms.meaning: One blessing (here, one of the three verses of ברכת כהנים)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, בל תוסיף applies only within a מצוה's time. The ברייתא about the כהן fits this rule, because he added his own ברכה after finishing only one of the three ברכות, while the מצוה was still ongoing.

phrases.english: He finished one blessing.
phrases.notes: Two more ברכות of ברכת כהנים remain, so he is still mid-מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17 by reinterpreting the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'סיים' means he finished all of ברכת כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'סיים' means he finished one ברכה only, so he was still within the מצוה's time.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the כהן finished all his blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 18 with a ברייתא that says the כהן finished ALL his blessings, not just one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: he finished all of his blessings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. That answer said 'finished' means he finished only one of the three blessings. Now a ברייתא says he finished all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 tried to keep the כהן inside the מצוה's time by saying two blessings were still left. This ברייתא says nothing was left. So the כהן added after the blessing was over, yet the ברייתא still says he violated בל תוסיף, which seems to contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
He finished
All of his blessings (all three verses of ברכת כהנים)

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: Standard opening for a challenge from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: He finished all of his blessings!
phrases.notes: Not just one blessing, but all three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 18's reading that 'finished' meant only one blessing.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 18's claim that the כהן had finished only one blessing, and behind it רבא's rule from Step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the כהן finished all three blessings, the מצוה is over. Adding then is outside its time, yet the ברייתא says he violated בל תוסיף.

steps.title: ברכת כהנים can be repeated, so its time is the whole day
steps.stepSummary: ברכת כהנים is different. A כהן who meets another congregation may bless again, so the entire day is its time, and adding at any point counts as adding within the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different. If another congregation happens to come to him, he goes back and blesses again. So the whole day is its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says ברכת כהנים has a special kind of time: the whole day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after finishing all three blessings, the כהן could still bless another congregation that same day. That shows the מצוה's time has not ended. So when he adds his own blessing, he is adding within the time, and רבא's rule from Step 14 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different
It happens to come his way
Another congregation
The whole day is its time

steps.confusionAlert: Finishing the blessing does NOT end the מצוה's time here. 'Time' means the period in which the מצוה can still be done, not the moment you stop doing it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines 'within its time' for בל תוסיף: if a מצוה can still be repeated that day, the day is still its time.

phrases.english: Here it is different,
since if there happens to come to him
another congregation,
he goes back and blesses again —
the whole day is its time.
phrases.notes: So adding even after finishing is still adding within the time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (שאני): the time of ברכת כהנים is the whole day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the כהן finished all three blessings, the מצוה's time was over.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because he can bless another congregation, the whole day is its time, so his addition is within the time and רבא's rule holds.

steps.title: A source from a משנה about mixed sacrificial blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for its principle that a מצוה which could be repeated that day has the whole day as its time. It quotes a משנה: blood of two one-sprinkling offerings that got mixed is sprinkled once, and blood of two four-sprinkling offerings is sprinkled four times.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say this? As we learned in a משנה: blood that needs one sprinkling that got mixed with blood that needs one sprinkling is sprinkled once. Blood that needs four sprinklings mixed with blood that needs four sprinklings is sprinkled four times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source and starts quoting a משנה. This step only gives the simple, agreed cases. It is setting up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some offerings need one sprinkling of blood on the מזבח, and some need four. When both bloods need the same number, there is no problem: you sprinkle that number. The proof will come from the hard case, where the numbers do not match.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asks for a source)
As we learned in a משנה
One sprinkling of blood on the מזבח
Four sprinklings of blood on the מזבח
That became mixed

phrases.english: And from where do you say this —
As we learned in a משנה:
Blood that is put on with one sprinkling,
that got mixed with blood put on with one sprinkling —
is put on with one sprinkling.
Four sprinklings mixed with four sprinklings —
is put on with four sprinklings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבא's rule, the גמרא looks for a source for the principle about adding within a מצוה's time.
steps.raayaObject: The principle from Step 20: if a מצוה can be repeated later that day, the whole day counts as its time for בל תוסיף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about mixed sacrificial blood. The agreed cases are quoted first, and the disputed case follows.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about mismatched blood
steps.stepSummary: When four-sprinkling blood is mixed with one-sprinkling blood, רבי אליעזר says to sprinkle four times and רבי יהושע says to sprinkle once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four-sprinkling blood mixed with one-sprinkling blood: רבי אליעזר says it is sprinkled four times. רבי יהושע says it is sprinkled once.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the hard case, where the bloods need different numbers of sprinklings. Two תנאים disagree about what to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every sprinkling now carries both bloods. רבי אליעזר goes with the higher number so the four-sprinkling offering is fully done. רבי יהושע goes with the lower number so the one-sprinkling offering gets nothing extra.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who says to sprinkle four times
A תנא who says to sprinkle once
They should be put on (sprinkled)

phrases.english: Four sprinklings mixed with one sprinkling,
רבי אליעזר says:
It is put on with four sprinklings,
רבי יהושע says:
It is put on with one sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה with the disputed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed four-sprinkling and one-sprinkling blood: four sprinklings according to רבי אליעזר, one sprinkling according to רבי יהושע.

steps.title: Each side warns of בל תגרע or בל תוסיף
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says one sprinkling violates בל תגרע. רבי יהושע answers that four sprinklings violate בל תוסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: But he violates 'do not take away'! רבי יהושע said to him: But he violates 'do not add'!
steps.whatsHappening: Each תנא challenges the other's position. Each one points to a different Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only one sprinkling, the four-sprinkling offering is missing three, which is בל תגרע. With four sprinklings, the one-sprinkling offering (the בכור) gets three extra, which is בל תוסיף. In Step 27 the גמרא will point out that these extra sprinklings come after the בכור's one sprinkling is already done, and it uses this point for the 'whole day is its time' idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against taking away from a מצוה
Violates
He said to him (a back-and-forth argument)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע treats the extra sprinklings on the בכור's blood as בל תוסיף, even though they come after its one required sprinkling is done. Step 27 builds its proof on exactly this point.
steps.confusionAlert: בל תגרע (taking away) and בל תוסיף (adding) are two separate prohibitions. Here they pull in opposite directions, and that is why the case is so hard.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר said to him:
But he is violating 'do not take away'!
phrases.notes: The four-sprinkling offering would be missing three sprinklings.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע said to him:
But he is violating 'do not add'!
phrases.notes: The one-sprinkling offering would get three extra sprinklings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תִּגְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning each תנא uses to challenge the other's ruling in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Each תנא's ruling: רבי יהושע's single sprinkling and רבי אליעזר's four sprinklings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sprinkling once takes away from the four-sprinkling offering (בל תגרע). Sprinkling four times adds to the one-sprinkling offering (בל תוסיף).

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: בל תוסיף Applies Only to Unmixed Blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע's objection. He says בל תוסיף only applies when the blood stands by itself, not when it is mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: The rule 'Do not add' was only said when the blood is by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his ruling of four sprinklings. He says adding to mixed blood does not break בל תוסיף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 23, רבי יהושע said four sprinklings would break בל תוסיף for the בכור's blood. רבי אליעזר answers that בל תוסיף was said only about unmixed blood. Once the blood is mixed, sprinkling extra for the sake of the other offering is not counted as adding.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against adding to a מצוה
When it is by itself (not mixed)
It was not said (the rule only applies to)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
'Do not add' was not stated
except when it is by itself.
phrases.notes: Meaning: when the blood is not mixed with other blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: לֹא נֶאֱמַר ״בַּל תּוֹסִיף״ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's challenge from Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four sprinklings break בל תוסיף for the one-sprinkling בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: בל תוסיף applies only to unmixed blood, so in a mixture four sprinklings are allowed.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Then בל תגרע Also Applies Only to Unmixed Blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע turns רבי אליעזר's own argument against him. If בל תוסיף applies only to unmixed blood, then בל תגרע should also apply only to unmixed blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: The rule 'Do not diminish' was also only said when the blood is by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע uses the same reasoning in reverse. If mixing cancels the problem of adding, it should also cancel the problem of taking away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's argument cuts both ways. If mixed blood is outside בל תוסיף, it is equally outside בל תגרע. Then one sprinkling is no longer a problem, and רבי אליעזר's reason for requiring four sprinklings falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against taking away from a מצוה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
'Do not diminish' was not stated
except when it is by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לֹא נֶאֱמַר ״בַּל תִּגְרַע״ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אליעזר's own reasoning from Step 24 against him.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר's answer as one-sided.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reasoning about mixed blood must apply to both prohibitions equally, so it cannot be used to favor four sprinklings.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Better to Fail by Doing Nothing than by Acting
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע gives another reason. Not sprinkling breaks בל תגרע passively, while sprinkling breaks בל תוסיף through an action. Doing nothing is better.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said further: If you do not sprinkle, you break 'Do not diminish,' but you did nothing with your hand. If you sprinkle, you break 'Do not add,' and you did an action with your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע adds a second argument for sprinkling only once. If a rule will be broken either way, it is better to break it without doing an action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if both choices break a rule, they are not equal. Holding back from sprinkling is only a failure to act (שב ואל תעשה). Sprinkling extra is an active violation. So sprinkling once is the better choice. This ends the quote from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An act done with your own hand (an active deed)
You sprinkled (literally: you put the blood)
And furthermore (an added argument)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's main point: when breaking a rule cannot be avoided, a passive violation is better than an active one.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that doing nothing (שב ואל תעשה) is better than an active violation is a well-known principle that appears throughout שס.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua said further:
When you did not sprinkle, you broke 'Do not diminish'
but you did not do an act with your hand;
when you sprinkled, you broke 'Do not add'
and you did an act with your hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second argument supporting רבי יהושע's ruling of one sprinkling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע's ruling to sprinkle only once
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that a passive violation is better than an active one

steps.title: The גמרא Uses the משנה to Prove the Whole Day Is the מצוה's Time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that once the בכור's one sprinkling is done, its time seems to be over. Yet the משנה says extra sprinkling breaks בל תוסיף. This must be because another בכור could come that day, making the whole day its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, once he has given the one sprinkling of the בכור, its time has passed. Yet the משנה teaches that he breaks 'Do not add.' Is this not because we say: since he would sprinkle again if another בכור came his way, the whole day is its time?
steps.whatsHappening: This is why the משנה was quoted (Step 21). The גמרא now applies it to prove the principle from Step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once the one sprinkling is done, the מצוה seems finished, so adding should come after its time. Yet רבי יהושע says it breaks בל תוסיף. The גמרא explains this as with ברכת כהנים: the מצוה could happen again that day with another בכור, so the whole day counts as its time.

keyTerms.meaning: A sprinkling of blood (literally: a giving)
A firstborn animal offering, which needs only one sprinkling
Its time has passed
It happens to come his way
The whole day is its time

phrases.english: And here,
once he has given the one sprinkling of the firstborn,
its time has passed,
and yet it teaches that he breaks 'Do not add.'
Is it not because we say:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ מִתְרְמֵי לֵיהּ בּוּכְרָא אַחֲרִינָא —
phrases.english: since if another firstborn happened to come his way,
he would sprinkle from it again,
the whole day is its time?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ מַתָּנָה מִבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the משנה and returns to the principle from Step 20 to prove it.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that if a מצוה can be repeated that day, the whole day is its time for בל תוסיף
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about mixed blood, where רבי יהושע says adding to the בכור's blood breaks בל תוסיף

steps.title: Rejection: רבי יהושע May Hold that Adding Is Forbidden Even After the Time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe רבי יהושע simply holds that בל תוסיף applies even outside a מצוה's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps רבי יהושע holds that one breaks the rule against adding to מצוות even outside their time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from Step 27. It offers another way to explain רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that adding after a מצוה's time is not a problem, so the time must stretch through the whole day. But רבי יהושע may simply hold that adding is forbidden even after the time. If so, the משנה shows nothing about the whole day being the time.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?
Perhaps
Outside their proper time

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the mixed-blood משנה fails. רבי יהושע may hold that בל תוסיף applies even outside a מצוה's time, so the משנה does not prove the 'whole day is its time' principle.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not rejecting the principle from Step 20 itself. It only rejects this משנה as proof for it.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps Rabbi Yehoshua holds
that one transgresses regarding מצוות (by adding)
even outside their time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not the principle itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed adding outside a מצוה's time is allowed. רבי יהושע may hold that it is forbidden even then.

steps.title: Why did רב שמן בר אבא skip the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies why it quoted the משנה about blood. It was not trying to prove רבי יהושע's view. It was asking why רב שמן בר אבא challenged רבא from a ברייתא instead of from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we meant: Why did רב שמן בר אבא leave aside the משנה and challenge from a ברייתא? He should have challenged from the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the rejection in step 28 by saying, 'That is not what we meant.' It explains the real reason it brought the משנה, and this sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28 the גמרא's proof was pushed aside. Now the גמרא says its point was different. A משנה is usually a stronger source than a ברייתא, so it is surprising that רב שמן built his challenge on the ברייתא about ברכת כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we were saying (a clarification of what we meant earlier)
Leaves aside, abandons
Raises a challenge
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not changing the subject. It is explaining that its earlier point was about רב שמן's choice of source, not about proving רבי יהושע's opinion.

phrases.english: This is what we were saying:

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא מַאי טַעְמָא
phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba, what is the reason
that he left aside the mishna and raised an objection from a baraita?
Let him object from the mishna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 28 by reframing the purpose of the earlier argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the purpose of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גמרא cited the משנה to prove that רבי יהושע holds the whole day is the מצוה's time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גמרא cited the משנה to ask why רב שמן did not challenge from it.

steps.title: The same answer should also push aside the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן avoided the משנה because it can be answered: another בכור might come, so the whole day is the time. But then the ברייתא can be answered the same way: another ציבור might come, so the whole day is the time for ברכת כהנים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why didn't he challenge from the משנה? Because if another בכור happened to come to him, he would have to sprinkle its blood, so the whole day is its time. But the same is true of the ברייתא: if another ציבור came along, the כהן would bless again, so the whole day is its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב שמן avoided the משנה. It then turns that same reasoning against the ברייתא he did use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about the בכור is weak as a challenge, because the whole day counts as the sprinkling's time. But the ברייתא has the same weakness: a כהן can bless another ציבור later that day. So the ברייתא's case also happens during the מצוה's time, and רב שמן's challenge seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Happens to come along by chance
A firstborn animal (בכור)
Sprinkles (the blood on the מזבח)
The whole day is its time
A congregation

phrases.english: What is the reason he does not object from the mishna?

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ מִתְרְמֵי לֵיהּ בּוּכְרָא אַחֲרִינָא
phrases.english: Because if another firstborn happened to come his way,
he would need to sprinkle from it;
so the whole day is its time.
The baraita as well:
since if another congregation happens along,
he blesses again;
the whole day is its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29, then uses that answer to undermine the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמן בר אבא's challenge to רבא from the ברייתא of ברכת כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason that weakens the משנה (more cases may come later that day) applies equally to the ברייתא.

steps.title: Required sprinkling versus optional blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן's defense: sprinkling another בכור's blood is a must, so the whole day truly is its time. Blessing another ציבור is optional, so after the first blessing the time has really ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שמן בר אבא, how would he answer? There, with the blood, he has no choice but to sprinkle. Here, with the blessing, if he wants he blesses, and if he wants he does not bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב שמן's choice of the ברייתא. It shows a real difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If another בכור comes, the כהן must sprinkle its blood, so the whole day is truly the time of that מצוה. A כהן only has to bless once a day, so blessing another ציבור is optional. That means the time of his obligation is over, and the ברייתא remains a good challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible not to; there is no choice but to
Gives, puts (the blood)
If he wants

phrases.english: And Rav Shemen bar Abba, how would he respond?
There, it is impossible for him not to put the blood.
Here, if he wishes, he blesses;
if he wishes, he does not bless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב שמן against the challenge in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the cases (required versus optional)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases allow repeating later in the day, so in both the whole day is the time.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a required repetition makes the whole day the time. An optional one does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: a מצוה's 'time' is defined by when you are obligated, not just by when you are allowed to do it.

steps.title: רבא's new answer: breaking a rule needs intent
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer to אביי's challenge about sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני. Fulfilling a מצוה does not need intent, but breaking בל תוסיף does. Someone who sleeps in the סוכה on שמיני without meaning to do the מצוה does not break בל תוסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: To fulfill a מצוה, intent is not needed. To transgress, intent is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a fresh answer to אביי's challenge from Step 13, based on כוונה (intent) instead of the מצוה's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can fulfill a מצוה without intending to, but adding to a מצוה breaks בל תוסיף only if you meant the act as a מצוה. The person sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת has no such intent, so he does not get מלקות. The כהן who adds his own ברכה clearly intends it, so the ברייתא saying he transgresses fits this answer too.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill one's obligation (יוצא)
To transgress
Intent to do the act as a מצוה

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר, לָצֵאת — לָא בָּעֵי כַּוָּונָה,
phrases.english: Rava said: To fulfill, intent is not required;
to transgress, intent is required.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, לָצֵאת לָא בָּעֵי כַּוָּונָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to אביי's challenge in Step 13, in place of the time-based answer of Step 14 that רב שמן challenged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fulfilling a מצוה does not require intent; breaking בל תוסיף requires intent.

steps.title: Blood sprinkling breaks the rule without intent
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: according to רבי יהושע, adding extra blood sprinklings breaks בל תוסיף even with no special intent. So breaking the rule does not always need intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about putting the blood, according to רבי יהושע? There one transgresses even without intent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's new rule using the blood sprinkling case from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע holds that extra sprinklings break בל תוסיף. He says nothing about the כהן needing to intend them as a מצוה. That contradicts רבא's claim that breaking the rule always needs intent.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at (opening a challenge)
Putting the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: But the putting of blood, according to Rabbi Yehoshua,
where one transgresses and intent is not required!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rule from step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that breaking בל תוסיף requires intent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רבי יהושע's blood sprinkling case, the rule is broken without any stated intent.

steps.title: רבא refines: intent matters only outside the מצוה's time
steps.stepSummary: רבא revises his rule. Fulfilling a מצוה never needs intent. Breaking בל תוסיף during the מצוה's time needs no intent, as with the blood. Outside the מצוה's time, breaking it needs intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: To fulfill, intent is not needed. To transgress during its time, intent is not needed. Not during its time, intent is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by narrowing his rule. Intent is needed only for breaking בל תוסיף outside the מצוה's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood sprinkling happens during its time, since the whole day is its time, so no intent is needed to break the rule there. Outside the time, the extra act looks like an ordinary action, so it counts as adding to the מצוה only if done with intent. That covers sleeping in a סוכה on שמיני עצרת, which is after the time of סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, he said (a revised version of a statement)
During its proper time
Not during its proper time

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final rule: (1) fulfilling a מצוה does not need intent; (2) breaking בל תוסיף during the מצוה's time does not need intent; (3) breaking בל תוסיף outside the מצוה's time does need intent.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. 'No intent needed' to fulfill a מצוה is a separate rule from the question of when you break בל תוסיף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why sitting in a סוכה on שמיני עצרת is a problem only if done with intent to fulfill the מצוה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
To fulfill, intent is not required.
To transgress, in its time, intent is not required;
not in its time, intent is required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Revises רבא's rule from step 32 to answer the challenge in step 33.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Breaking בל תוסיף always requires intent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Breaking בל תוסיף requires intent only outside the מצוה's time.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Intent is needed only for breaking בל תוסיף outside the מצוה's time. Inside its time, and for fulfilling a מצוה, no intent is needed.

steps.title: רבי זירא speaks to his attendant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new report: רבי זירא said something to his attendant. This line only sets up his instruction, which follows on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to his attendant:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is introducing something רבי זירא told his attendant, and his actual words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just finished רבא's rule that fulfilling a מצוה does not need intent. Now the גמרא turns to a report about רבי זירא and his attendant, connected to intent in the מצוה of שופר. What he tells his attendant will show how he felt about the need for כוונה. Hold the question in mind: does it agree with רבא or not?

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him
רבי זירא, an אמורא
His attendant or servant (here, the one who blew שופר for him)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a ruling in this line. It is only the opening of a quote. The point comes in the next words.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to his attendant:
phrases.notes: The colon shows that his instruction follows next, about blowing שופר with intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's final rule (Step 34) that fulfilling a מצוה needs no intent, the גמרא brings a new report about רבי זירא that touches the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an opening line for a quote. רבי זירא's instruction to his attendant follows on the next amud.
